description: What the window is allowed to do. Deliberately small: folder picking, the three read-only tool commands, and a notification the window may raise while it is in the background. The global-shortcut plugin is initialised in lib.rs but its own commands are deliberately not listed here, so the only chord that can ever be registered is the one a person set in Settings, through set_global_shortcut. Webview zoom is the one webview permission: it scales the page the app already draws, and is the only way a terminal's text stays sharp when it grows, because CSS zoom would scale xterm's canvas as a bitmap. The notification plugin is listed by the three permissions it actually needs rather than by notification:default, because that set also grants register-action-types and register-listener — buttons on the banner and a handler for them, which is the one thing a Vylo notification must never have. See the header of src/notify.ts.
